evals.prompt: refactor the api to use sqlalchemy
evals.expected_output: models.py and db.py are created, app.py endpoints use Depends(get_db) and the ORM, old raw-SQL helpers are removed, tests are migrated, and pytest passes.
expectations: models.py defines PredictionSession and DetectionObject as declarative SQLAlchemy models with correct column types.
db.py defines engine, SessionLocal, get_db() generator, and init_db() calling Base.metadata.create_all.
Every database-touching endpoint in app.py has db: Session = Depends(get_db).
app.py contains no import sqlite3, no conn.execute, no raw SQL strings, no DB_PATH.
pytest tests/ passes with all tests green and no regression in coverage.
DetectionObject model includes indexes idx_prediction_uid, idx_label, idx_score.

evals.prompt: add an endpoint GET /predictions/recent that returns the 10 most recent sessions
evals.expected_output: A new GET /predictions/recent endpoint queries sessions ordered by timestamp descending limited to 10, using the ORM. A test covers ordering and the limit.
expectations: app.py has a GET /predictions/recent route with db: Session = Depends(get_db).
The query uses .order_by(PredictionSession.timestamp.desc()).limit(10) with no raw SQL.
Returns a list of session objects with uid, timestamp, original_image, predicted_image.
At least one new test asserts at most 10 results and most-recent-first ordering.
pytest tests/ passes and no existing endpoint behaviour changed.

evals.prompt: add a UserFeedback table to track user ratings per prediction
evals.expected_output: A UserFeedback SQLAlchemy model is added to models.py, the table is created via create_all, and endpoints to create and read feedback are added with 404 if the prediction does not exist.
expectations: models.py defines UserFeedback with at least id, prediction_uid, and rating columns.
No hand-written CREATE TABLE is added.
New endpoints use db: Session = Depends(get_db) and return 404 for unknown prediction uid.
Tests cover create, read, and not-found paths.
pytest tests/ passes and no existing endpoint is changed.

evals.prompt: add a column processing_time_ms to the prediction_sessions table
evals.expected_output: A nullable processing_time_ms column is added to PredictionSession, populated in POST /predict, with a note that existing Postgres tables need a real migration.
expectations: PredictionSession gains processing_time_ms with a numeric type and nullable=True.
POST /predict stores the value before db.commit().
No raw ALTER TABLE or SQL string is added.
Agent flags that create_all does not alter existing tables in production.
pytest tests/ passes and existing response shapes are unchanged.

evals.prompt: delete a prediction session and all its detection objects by uid
evals.expected_output: A DELETE endpoint removes the session and its detection objects via the ORM in one transaction, returns 404 for unknown uid, covered by tests.
expectations: app.py has a DELETE /prediction/{uid} route with db: Session = Depends(get_db).
Handler deletes DetectionObject rows then PredictionSession row then db.commit().
Unknown uid returns 404 matching existing error style.
No raw SQL is used.
Tests cover successful delete and 404 path, pytest passes.

evals.prompt: make the database backend configurable so we can use postgres in production
evals.expected_output: db.py selects SQLite or Postgres from DB_BACKEND env var, check_same_thread only for SQLite, psycopg2-binary added to requirements, app behaviour identical on both backends.
expectations: db.py reads DB_BACKEND and builds postgresql:// or sqlite:/// URL accordingly.
connect_args check_same_thread is only applied for SQLite.
requirements.txt gains psycopg2-binary and sqlalchemy.
No endpoint code in app.py changes to switch backends.
pytest tests/ passes and agent describes how to verify with Docker Postgres.
